findings.claim: The landmark_00 soft-mass curve over the observed support [0.0,0.49] rises from a negative early value to a positive mid-window plateau and then declines back toward negative at the last node, with four sign changes and no accepted polynomial, so it is oscillatory rather than a monotone staged drift.

The landmark_00 soft-mass curve has large opposing first-node and last-node rate z-scores while its whole-window z is small, so the endpoint cloud is not drifting monotonically in this coordinate across the window.

Landmark_00 local shape coordinates show multiple sign changes and strong sign conflicts with no accepted polynomial, indicating oscillatory rather than staged monotone coordinate change over the window.

The learning window and observed score nodes span 0.0 to 0.5 with 50 evenly spaced score clocks, and the objective is final predicted target affinity primary with coordinate control only, so any coordinate reward must be evaluated against endpoint affinity rather than treated as the objective itself.

hypotheses.direction: test registered temporal_recipe levels at fixed dose_factors=1; do not reverse the affinity objective
hypotheses.falsifier: if the compiled schedule produces no change in realized per-node coordinate traces, or if endpoint affinity does not improve relative to the constant-curvature control, the stage-dependent hypothesis is not supported
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_soft_mass curve values and rate z-scores across observed score nodes
hypotheses.statement: A stage-dependent curvature schedule (registered C1/C2/C3 recipes) may be worth testing at fixed dose because the landmark_00 soft-mass curve changes sign and slope within the window, so a single constant curvature may not match the observed early-versus-late contrast.

hypotheses.direction: retain constant curvature unless a registered time-varying recipe shows a reproducible trace change
hypotheses.falsifier: if C2 and a time-varying recipe yield indistinguishable coordinate traces, the time-varying edit is not justified
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_soft_mass whole-window z and sign-change count
hypotheses.statement: Because the landmark_00 soft-mass curve shows no net whole-window trend while oscillating within the window, a constant-curvature control (C2) is a reasonable baseline against which any time-varying curvature must demonstrate a measurable trace difference.

limitations: Stage profiles and temporal profiles are unavailable; only continuous curves and trend tables were read.
No decoded final affinity labels are present in role input, so selection preference and coordinate trends cannot be equated with measured final benefit.
Coordinate features are untyped predicted-endpoint world-coordinate proxies; no energy or chemical-interaction interpretation is made.
Only the landmark_00_soft_mass curve was read directly; other landmark_00 features rest on continuous_trends summary rows.
